[2026-08-19 | AMZN | Underweight | -2.1% | -1.7% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Underweight: trim 40–50% of a full single-name exposure now, taking a standard 5% position to roughly 2.5–3.0% of portfolio. Execute the first tranche at/near the $265.84 close rather than waiting for a rally, and leave a working limit in the $271.58–$272.65 VWMA/supply shelf for any residual strength. Do not initiate a new long and do not short at $265.84; the tactical overlay is optional and trigger-only on a daily close below $257.73 on >40M shares, capped at half the trader's maximum (≤0.25–0.5% portfolio risk, stop $266.50) or expressed as a defined-risk put. De-risk the residual on closes below $257.73 (~25% of standard) and $249.00 (structural failure, $238.22 target); restore in two steps — 3.5–4.0% only on a close above $272.65 on ≥48M shares with the MACD histogram recrossing zero, full weight only after the Q3 capex/margin/D&A/deferred-revenue/mark checks. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the late-October print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not in dispute: the Research Manager, the trader, and all three risk seats converge on reducing AMZN, and the aggressive analyst is right that this is the rare debate where the "aggressive" action and the prudent action are the same trade. What decided the call is that the aggressive analyst won the two arguments that set the multiple, the conservative won execution and gap risk, and the neutral won the structure of the response.

The aggressive analyst wins on cash-flow and earnings quality, and neither colleague refuted it. TTM free cash flow is –$11.6B against +$13.5B a year earlier; H1 FCF is –$27.0B against a $173B TTM capex run-rate; Q2 D&A is only 37% of Q2 capex and TTM D&A only 43% of TTM capex, so the 1.3–2.0 point annual margin headwind is still ahead — the "Q2 already absorbed it" defense fails because Q2 D&A depreciates prior-year assets, not the current surge. Cash taxes of $4.0B on $120.7B of H1 pretax income flatter the $161.4B OCF headline by roughly $30B, leaving a mid-30s core multiple on core EPS near $1.96 rather than the reported $5.75. Lease-adjusted the balance sheet is roughly –$66.7B net debt, not net cash, and the $122.3B non-marketable equity book — up 655% in six months, ~11% of assets, driving $62.8B of H1 pre-tax upward adjustments — is correlated beta to the same AI narrative that supports the multiple, not free optionality. Negative FCF plus a mid-30s core multiple plus no buyback and no dividend is no margin of safety.

The tape reinforces the trim rather than refuting it. AMZN at $265.84 closed below the $271.91 VWMA, so the dollar-weighted buyer of the last ~20 sessions is underwater — precisely why every rally from 08-04 to 08-11 died in the $271.58–$278.09 shelf. The lower-high sequence $287.20 → $280.14 → $266.40 is intact, the 08-17 MACD bear cross is still in force (histogram –0.8817, line down five sessions from 8.43 to 4.81), the 08-19 reversal printed 35.76M shares against a ~48.2M average (~71%), and an unfilled gap from roughly $231.06 to $265.00 sits directly beneath price. A bullish outside day on 71% volume into a shelf that has rejected three times is a bounce, not a reversal.

But the aggressive overreaches in three places and the conservative and neutral are right to cut him back. The anatomy is not bearish enough for a directional short: price is 11.59% above a rising 200 SMA ($238.22), 6.8% above a rising 50 SMA ($249.00) the pullback never tested, RSI is 55.64 mid-range with no confirmed divergence, the MACD line is still positive at 4.81, and the 08-19 session held the higher low ($258.58 vs $257.73) and reclaimed the 10 EMA ($264.46). The overlay as proposed is not "cheap convexity": with ATR at 7.86 (2.95% of spot) the $266.50 stop is only ~1.1 ATR above the $257.73 trigger, so a stop-run through the $258.58–$259.45 confluence is as likely as the gap-fill — it is a new volatility exposure and must be half-sized or expressed as a defined-risk put. And treating the missing Form 4 data as a bearish certainty is wrong; it is an information gap, and the correct response to an unknown is less exposure, not a second way to lose money.

I side with the conservative and neutral on execution: AMZN gapped $235.50 → $265.00 overnight in late July, and the largest identified tail — a markdown against a $122.3B model-valued book — is exactly a gap event that will not politely print $257.73 so a trigger can fire. So the reduction does not depend on reaching $271.58; the first tranche executes near the $265.84 close with a limit left in the shelf. Where I side with the neutral against the conservative is restoration: requiring a $272.65/48M close plus every fundamental gate plus insider review before any weight returns converts a tactical underweight into permanent avoidance of a business still compounding operating income at +43.2% on a 13.7% margin with +19.6% revenue growth. The two-stage gate is the correct compromise.

That is why the rating is Underweight and not Sell. A Sell abandons a franchise whose operating engine is accelerating and whose primary structure — rising 50 and 200 SMA, uninterrupted higher low — has not failed, and the record is unambiguous that full exits and heavy underweights on AMZN in this cycle (07-22 through 07-30) cost between 12% and 22% of five-day alpha. The mirror lessons are live too: the 08-12 Underweight produced –0.1% alpha and the 08-11 Hold –4.3%, and the cross-ticker AAPL lesson warns specifically that an Underweight whose falsification level sits only ~2.6% above spot (here $272.65 vs $265.84) has poor expectancy unless a real core is retained. Keeping 2.5–3.0% rather than exiting respects both.

What would change it. Upward: a close above $272.65 on ≥48M shares with the MACD histogram recrossing zero restores 3.5–4.0%; full weight requires Q3 capex flat or down, operating margin ≥13.7% with D&A/revenue ≥10.5%, deferred revenue growing off the flat ~$24.9B (against receivables +30.1% on revenue +19.6%), and non-marketable equity flat or positive. Downward: a close below $257.73 on >40M takes the core to ~25% of standard and legitimizes the half-sized overlay; a close below $249.00 confirms structural failure toward $238.22, at which point the thesis is being validated by price and the residual should be re-underwritten, not defended.

Explicit gaps I am not underwriting: no Form 4/insider data, so insider behavior cannot be scored in either direction; no AWS segment revenue, margin or backlog, so the AWS thesis and the demand side of a $173B capex program are unvalidated; no organic-versus-acquired revenue split despite a large acquisition program; no consensus, peer comps or valuation multiples, so the 34–36x core multiple is report-derived arithmetic rather than a computed screen; and no portfolio, holdings or cash context, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation and should flex with whatever other AI-capex exposure the caller already carries.

**Price Target**: 252.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
Five-day alpha of -1.7% (raw -2.1% vs SPY) means the Underweight call was directionally right, but five sessions cannot validate a 3–6 month thesis built on FCF and core earnings — treat it as tape confirmation only. What it supports is the execution half of the argument: refusing to wait for the $271.58 shelf and taking the first tranche at the $265.84 close, with the lower-high sequence and sub-VWMA close playing out as written; the FCF/D&A/core-multiple case remains untested until the Q3 print. Lesson for next time: when the falsification level sits only ~2.6% above spot, the trim's alpha arrives fast and is easily mistaken for thesis confirmation — keep the at-market first tranche, but pre-commit to judging the fundamental leg only at the scheduled catalyst.

[2026-08-18 | AMZN | Overweight | +0.6% | +0.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Build AMZN toward 1.0-1.1x a standard allocation (moderating the 1.2-1.3x initially proposed) via a staged, confirmation-gated entry. Take 15% of the intended full position at market (~259.45), then earn the rest: 25-30% on a daily close reclaiming 264.15 and then 267.27 (VWMA) on volume above 45M shares; 25-30% on a two-session hold of 253.00-257.68 with RSI not breaking 40; the final 25-30% on a held retest of 248.59. Do not run the original mechanical 30/40/30 ladder, which commits 70% into the approach to the 248.59-239.82 air pocket while forbidding averaging down. Hard tripwire 247.60 on tranche one; a daily close below 248.59 halts all adds; a daily close below 239.82 cuts back to at least standard weight rather than widening the stop for a losing add. No new tranche in the two sessions around WMT (Aug 20) or NVDA Q2. Cash equity only, no leverage or options, given a 3.03% daily ATR and two double-digit overnight gaps in seven months. Horizon 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction belongs to the bulls; sizing and mechanics belong to the bears. The undisputed operating evidence is decisive: Q2 revenue +19.6% against total cost growth of 16.6% — a ~300bp positive spread — with operating income +43.2% to $27.46B at a 13.69% margin (+230bp), every major cost line running slower than revenue (COGS 18.5%, other opex 16.3%, marketing +2.5%, G&A -6.0%, SBC -7.6%), and core EPS still up ~29% in Q2 and ~26% in H1 after stripping the marks. The point the conservative never neutralized: depreciation rose ~42% and D&A ~32% while margins expanded 230bp, so prior capex vintages are demonstrably earning. His counter — capex at 2.3x D&A ($173.0B vs $75.2B) means the catch-up is still ahead — is a real durability and proof-standard worry, but it is a limit on size, not evidence of deterioration. The absolute position is not distressed: $176.1B of cash and AFS securities, net cash still positive at +$29.7B, 20.9x interest coverage, $133.0B of investment-grade debt raised to pre-position power, land and silicon.

The bears won four exchanges and all four are carried into execution. Deferred tax of $41.4B against $6.6B of cash taxes in the TTM means the "+33% operating cash flow" and the Level-3 marks are partly the same phenomenon, and the bull never answered it. Net cash fell from +$51.5B to +$29.7B in six months, long-term debt went $68.8B to $133.0B, interest expense doubled, the current ratio is 1.03x, and two to three more quarters at the H1 burn crosses zero. The $650.03B of contractual obligations is a cost commitment, not revenue: contract liabilities are flat at ~$24.88B while the commitments are overwhelmingly purchase obligations in AI compute, chips and energy, with $78.1B due inside twelve months — the aggressive analyst's "backlog with a price tag" inverts the sign of the largest fixed-cost line. And the tape is broken short-term: a lower high at 278.09 against 284.02, the heaviest volume day of the slide (43.9M) printing a new low and the first close below the July 31 session low of 262.01, price 1.78% under the 10-EMA (264.1475) on four straight closes below it and 2.9% under a still-rising VWMA (267.2688) where trapped supply sits, MACD histogram -0.9082 after the 08-17 bearish cross, and only 0.69% above the 257.68 pivot that today's 257.73 low essentially tagged.

That breakdown does not force Hold. The three losing AMZN calls in this book — the 08-06 Overweight (raw -2.6%) and the 08-05 and 08-11 Holds (raw -2.0%, -4.7%) — all failed on one defect: entering or parking a constructive rating while price sat 5.5%-12% above its 10-EMA in the 272-278 zone after a +25% three-session repricing. This is not that setup. At 259.45 AMZN is 8.65% off its high, below its 10-EMA, 4.4% above a 50-SMA (248.5854) that bottomed at 246.3842 on 07-30 and has risen 13 straight sessions, and 9.0% above a monotonically rising 200-SMA at 238.0085 with no death-cross risk. Reward-to-risk has flipped: ~4.6% to the 247.60 tripwire against ~9.5% to the 284.02 high. The 08-10 Underweight, the best recent call (+6.0%), worked because it led with that arithmetic and pre-committed structural exits; the 08-11 reflection's lesson was not to park a one-sided setup at Hold again.

Overriding the plan and the trader on mechanics, per the conservative and neutral seats: a 30% first tranche is too large for a name that printed a 222.69-to-202.70 (~9%) and a 235.50-to-265.00 (+12.5%) overnight gap in seven months, and the ladder as written is self-contradictory — it forbids averaging down into the gap shelf while committing 70% of the position into 253.00-248.59 and then widening the stop to 239.82 if that tranche fills, making real risk north of 4% of intended size before slippage rather than the quoted 1.4%. Hence 10-15% initial, adds earned by a confirmed reclaim or a held retest, and a 1.0-1.1x cap. I also reject the aggressive analyst's reliance on a June 30 13F, a self-described "unverified" Anthropic run-rate, and a Morgan Stanley headline with no target or estimates.

What would move me to Buy: sequential capex at or below Q2's $54.2B with operating margin holding at least 13% — that single capex line is the re-rating catalyst. What would move me to Underweight: operating margin below 13% while capex steps above $58B sequentially, or a reported EPS miss on a private-AI mark-down, since $62.8B of H1 mark-up is 52% of H1 net income against a $122.3B Level-3 book that grew from $16.2B at year-end. Unexamined and not underweighted: no analyst price target, no estimate-revision data, no independently confirmed Anthropic figure, and no portfolio or cash context, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard allocation. The July 31 gap implies an unscheduled catalyst absent from every dataset here; a fresh fundamental surprise invalidates this framework and requires re-underwriting before any further tranche.

**Price Target**: 285.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
Five days gave +0.6% raw and +0.8% alpha versus SPY — mildly supportive of the Overweight direction, but far too short a window to validate or falsify a 3-6 month capex-earning thesis; all it shows is that the short-term breakdown did not extend. That supports the specific piece the call rested on: at 259.45 price was below the 10-EMA but 4.4% above a rising 50-SMA, the 247.60 tripwire was never approached, and the ~4.6%-down / ~9.5%-up reward-to-risk asymmetry held — though the 264.15 and 267.27 confirmation gates never triggered, so only the 15% starter tranche participated in the move. Lesson for next time: when the edge is arithmetic rather than tape-confirmed, the upper ladder rungs forfeit real participation on a drift higher — put the first add on a close above the 10-EMA rather than the VWMA with volume, and start the tranche nearer 20% of intended size.

[2026-08-17 | AMZN | Underweight | +0.3% | +1.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN at 261.31 is Underweight: reduce, do not exit, do not add. Trim roughly 35–40% of existing exposure in two tranches — half at or near the current reference or into any 263–265 bounce, half as a limit bid in the 265.19–265.50 supply cluster (10 EMA 265.19 / rising VWMA 265.27 / 38.2% retrace 265.49); if that limit does not fill and AMZN closes below 257.09, complete the remaining trim at market rather than waiting for a better bid the structure says will not come. Carry the residual at ~60–65% of a standard allocation, sized so a gap to the 248.32 (50 SMA) structural line costs no more than ~0.4–0.5% of equity, and assume slippage beyond any stop with ATR at 8.12 (3.1% of price). Escalate to 25–30% of standard weight on a close below 257.09 on >50M shares or two consecutive closes below it; a close below 248.32 takes the residual to tracking size. Rebuild only on two consecutive closes above 265.75 on volume above the 47.8M 21-session average with the MACD histogram turning positive — and then only to 80–90% of standard with the risk point reset at 257.6.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is settled; the debate is about degree and execution. Three verifiable items decide it.

1) THE PAYOFF MAP IS NEGATIVE AND NOBODY CONTESTED IT. From 261.31 with the structural line at the 50 SMA (248.32), risk is 12.99 points (4.97%). The first two targets — 274.48 and 278.09 — pay only 1.01:1 and 1.29:1, and even the top of the range at 287.20 pays 1.99:1. Downside to the 237.9–239.8 gap-fill / 200-SMA confluence is ~9%. The aggressive analyst's advertised 3:1 required the bottom of the buy zone and the top of the target range simultaneously. The tape corroborates it one-sidedly: close below the 10 EMA (265.19), below the rising VWMA (265.27), rejection of the 265.75 session high, first negative MACD histogram (−0.310) since 2026-07-30, lowest close of the entire post-gap period, back inside the pre-gap range ceiling (~278.56), on 43.90M shares (1.33x the five-session average) on a down day, with RSI 52.43 leaving no oversold cushion. This is the same configuration that made the 2026-08-10 Underweight pay (−6.0% raw and alpha in five days), and that reflection's lesson is load-bearing: lead with the reward-to-risk arithmetic and pre-committed structural exits, and do not let stacked moving averages soften the trim.

2) EARNINGS QUALITY IS IMPAIRED AND THE BULL'S DEFENSE CONFLATED TWO THINGS. The $122.3B private-stake line (up from $16.2B in six months, ~21% of implied book equity, driving ~62% of Q2 EPS) is a Level-3 mark, not the aggressive analyst's \"hard, monetizable IPO catalyst\"; a 20% haircut is ~$24B pre-tax, larger than an entire quarter of operating income.
